outcome: Repair attempts inherit their predecessor's knowledge and degradation is loud: a retry or repair dispatch receives the prior try's submission summary and detail as explicit context, every continuation-rehydrate fallback records its reason, and a manifest degradation budget parks the run instead of letting silent context loss burn tokens indefinitely.

exclude: serializable cross-process continuation state (a future release)
changing the continuation contract's process-local design
telemetry controlling or recovering a run

acceptance.text: A repair or retry dispatch for a work item whose prior try submitted includes that submission's summary and detail in the worker's prepared context, proven by a test inspecting dispatch inputs; the ~40 turns per attempt measured reconstructing predecessor state (sworn#204) become unnecessary.

Every fresh_rehydrate.fallback event body names the reason rehydration failed (the labelled site from the ledger, or expiry, or absence), proven by tests provoking each; silence is no longer the rendering of context loss.

The manifest limits gain a bounded degradation budget (default: three rehydrate fallbacks per run); exceeding it parks the run at a safe boundary with a named reason listing the fallback events, proven end to end with a fake driver. The budget is runtime policy in the reducer, in the same class as try budgets - not telemetry.
Existing manifests without the new limit field admit unchanged with the documented default, and a manifest declaring the field round-trips through admission.

constraints: Every fallback path must either be loud or be forbidden (sworn#205); this slice makes the continuation fallback loud and budgeted, never forbidden.
Prior-submission context is worker input, not authority: it never substitutes for receipts and carries a provenance line naming the try it came from.
Evidence basis: 60% of dispatches lost context silently in r6/r7 (sworn#204); the parks and their costs are journaled in the 2026-08-12 and 2026-08-16 release runs.
The e2e check is declared, not executed by a role (ADR 0010).
Check evidence belongs in the submission's checks field, never in files added to the repository.
